message.content: {"answer": "E", "option_text": "The posteroanterior view shows tracheomegaly with ill-defined opacities predominantly in the right lower lobe and increased linear opacities in the left pulmonary base, consistent with cylindrical bronchiectasis.", "reason": "Visual inspection of Figure 1a (PA) confirms marked tracheomegaly (blue arrowheads) and patchy/ill-defined opacities in the right lower lung zone. Figure 1b (lateral) demonstrates prominent parallel linear opacities ('tram-tracking') at the lung bases, characteristic of cylindrical bronchiectasis associated with Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The report generator's claim of 'normal hilar contours' contradicts the obvious tracheal dilation and is overridden by pixel evidence (guided by t000006). Option E correctly synthesizes the PA findings (tracheomegaly + RLL opacities) with the lateral finding (basal linear opacities/bronchiectasis)."}
